blocks.title: Two-way tables: fix the denominator
blocks.basis: Concepts T2: Needs practice (2026-11-17 attempt chose row total for column percentage)
blocks.details: Use new table questions. Name the reference group first, divide by its total, then state the percentage to one decimal place with the group in words.

blocks.title: Loop comparisons: targeted variants
blocks.basis: Concepts P2: Needs practice (2026-11-17 attempt counted assignments and loop checks)
blocks.details: Trace new loops and report only element-to-element comparisons; explicitly exclude assignments, index updates, and loop-condition checks.

blocks.title: Bayes’ rule: locate course notes
blocks.basis: Concepts T3: Unassessed, in scope; teaching notes not posted
blocks.details: Find the lecture notes or request the instructor’s Bayes’ rule explanation before studying it. The outline alone does not provide a method to learn from.

blocks.title: Big-O: locate course notes
blocks.basis: Concepts P3: Unassessed, in scope; teaching notes not posted
blocks.details: Find the lecture notes or request the instructor’s Big-O explanation. The outline alone does not provide enough content for a course-grounded lesson.

blocks.title: Grouped summaries: learn from notes §3
blocks.basis: Concepts T4: Unassessed; teaching notes available in S2 §3
blocks.details: Review grouped summaries in STA/materials/notes.md §3. Explain one summary per non-empty group and compare like with like.

blocks.title: Nested data summaries: learn from notes §3
blocks.basis: Concepts P4: Unassessed; teaching notes available in P2 §3
blocks.details: Review nested list groups in CS/materials/notes.md §3. Work out the requested statistic separately for each inner list and label each group.

blocks.title: Conditional probability: unaided recheck
blocks.basis: Concepts T1: Demonstrated, Recheck before exam (promoted 2026-11-17)
blocks.details: Try a fresh question without notes. Identify the reference group, use its total as denominator, and report a one-decimal percentage with the group named.

blocks.title: List aliasing: transfer practice
blocks.basis: Concepts P1: Improving; transfer practice next (no transfer attempt yet)
blocks.details: Trace a new example with an alias or shallow copy. Draw which names share each list before mutation, then predict what changes are visible.

blocks.title: Grouped summaries: independent practice
blocks.basis: Concepts T4: Unassessed; in scope with notes available S2 §3
blocks.details: Without notes, summarize a new grouped dataset, showing one row per non-empty group and comparing the same statistic across groups.

blocks.title: Nested data summaries: independent practice
blocks.basis: Concepts P4: Unassessed; in scope with notes available P2 §3
blocks.details: For a new nested list, compute the requested statistic per inner list. State which observations belong to each result.

blocks.title: STAT 110: cumulative retrieval and practice
blocks.basis: Course scope T1–T4: in scope per STA/course-profile.md
blocks.details: Retrieve conditional probability, row/column percentages, and grouped summaries, then attempt available practice without the key. Revisit Bayes only if course notes have been found. Hypothesis testing is excluded.

blocks.title: CS 101: cumulative retrieval and practice
blocks.basis: Course scope P1–P4: in scope per CS/course-profile.md
blocks.details: Retrieve aliasing, loop tracing, and nested summaries, then attempt available practice without the key. Include Big-O only if course notes have been found. Recursion is excluded.

blocks.title: STAT 110: final light review
blocks.basis: Course scope T1–T4: in scope per STA/course-profile.md; T1 recheck due before exam
blocks.details: Briefly revisit any errors, especially denominators and the T1 reference group. Keep the last evening light before the 09:00 exam.

blocks.title: CS 101: final light review
blocks.basis: Course scope P1–P4: in scope per CS/course-profile.md
blocks.details: Review corrections and course reporting rules; do a short fresh comparison-count trace. Keep the last evening light before the 14:00 exam.
